title: Design System: AD Motors Mobile Services 24/7

board.purpose: The running-in board's lettering. Uppercase, stretched on the wdth axis to enamel-sign proportions. Nothing else uses it.

display.purpose: The hero headline, capped at 16ch, and the closing lever's number at board scale.

title.purpose: Service names in the frame rows and the value line of a block indication.

body.purpose: Running copy on iron at 1.62 line-height.

standfirst.purpose: The lead paragraph under a heading, in enamel-mid, capped 46-54ch.

label.purpose: Instrument labels, brass cell labels, engraved plate descriptions. Archivo with 0.2em tracking, never the mono.

measure.purpose: Martian Mono, confined to measurements: hour ring numerals, the live Derby time, and the frame's number plates.

shadows.name: enamel-sign
shadows.purpose: The running-in board and any full enamel field: a lit top lip, a dark bottom lip, one long drop.

shadows.name: brass-plate
shadows.purpose: Any bolted description plate at rest.

shadows.name: brass-plate-hover
shadows.purpose: The same plate under the pointer, paired with filter: brightness(1.07).

shadows.name: hung-disc
shadows.purpose: The target disc; the inset rings are its enamel border, not depth.

shadows.name: bolt-head
shadows.purpose: Brass bolts at the board's ends and rivets on every plate.

shadows.name: painted-stock
shadows.purpose: The lever handle, shadowed as a drawing so the shadow follows its silhouette.

shadows.name: lit-glass
shadows.purpose: A lamp with something behind it: block needles and the live hour on the ring. Glow is only ever emitted by lamp glass.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Every pointer response: plate brightness, border warmth, row wash, the lever's swing through its catch.

motion.name: ease-pull
motion.purpose: The signal arm coming off danger, delayed 1.1s. The page's one authored gesture.

motion.name: glass-cross
motion.purpose: Red glass out of the lamp, green glass in, once the arm has settled.

motion.name: reduced-motion-floor
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing moves and every state stays legible.

narrative.northStar: The Signal Box at Three in the Morning
narrative.overview:
Derby is the Midland Railway's works town, and signalling is the one trade whose entire point is that somebody is awake at three in the morning. That is the business, so the page is built out of the object rather than decorated with a reference to it: a vitreous enamel running-in board, a target disc hung off its end, a painted lever the visitor pulls, a lower quadrant semaphore that comes off danger, brass description plates bolted through, and a twenty-four hour clock face with every hour lit.

The system is material before it is graphic. Four materials carry everything and each one is allowed in exactly one place: enamel for maroon fields, iron for the ground, brass for plates and rules, lamp glass for state. Nothing is an accent colour; a maroon region is a piece of enamel signage, and a brass edge is a plate. The ground is a night, and because no photograph of this business exists and none may be invented, the night is drawn rather than shot: three hand-authored SVG light assets place a signal box window spilling onto ballast, re-authored per orientation instead of cover-cropped.

Density is signage density. Type sits at board proportions and stretches on Archivo's width axis rather than reaching for a second display face; measurements sit in Martian Mono and nowhere else. Depth is real casting depth, never a card stack. The confirmed anti-reference is the category's stock arrangement: a photograph of a smiling man in hi-vis beside an open bonnet under a red CALL NOW band, three icon cards and a tick list.
keyCharacteristics: Night iron ground with a single warm light source, drawn not photographed
Midland maroon enamel carrying whole regions, rendered as fired glass with specular sweep, speckle and chipped bolt holes
Brass for every description plate and rule, engraved dark, never a text colour on maroon
Two lamp glasses only, red for the visitor's state and green for what happens when they ring
Archivo on its width axis for signage; Martian Mono confined to measurements
One authored motion in the whole page: the arm pulling off danger

rules.name: The Whole Region Rule
rules.body: Maroon is a piece of enamel, not an accent. If a maroon area is smaller than a sign, it is wrong; tint it iron or leave it alone.

rules.name: The Two Glasses Rule
rules.body: Colour that reports state has exactly two values: red for the visitor's situation, green for the outcome of ringing. Nothing else on the page may signal by hue.

rules.name: The Brass Never Reads Rule
rules.body: Brass is a material edge, a rule, a plate face. It never sets running text on maroon, where it fails contrast. Letters on a brass plate are engraved dark (#1c1408).

rules.name: The Five Colour Exception
rules.body: The frame paint code appears on the lever stocks and their matching row spots only. Extending it to any other surface breaks a client authorisation, not a preference.

rules.name: The Instrument Voice Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono appears only where the page is reporting a measurement: the hour ring numerals, the live Derby time, and the frame's number plates. Never body copy, never a label, never a heading.

rules.name: The One Axis Rule
rules.body: Reach for Archivo's wdth axis before reaching for a second family. Board lettering stretches (108-112), display headings compress (96-98), and no other display face enters the system.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Any figure the visitor may read as a quantity, a time or a phone number is set with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so it does not shimmer when it updates.

rules.name: The Thumb Reach Rule
rules.body: Every way to ring is at least 44px tall and the primary lever is 66px, 54px in the call bar. On a 390px viewport a phone number is visible without scrolling and a second one is under the thumb.

rules.name: The Cast Edge Rule
rules.body: Depth is built from a 1px light inset at the top, a dark inset at the bottom, and one long soft drop. No hard offset shadow, and no shadow whose blur is smaller than its offset.

rules.name: The Glow Is A Lamp Rule
rules.body: A glow means something is lit. It belongs to lamp glass, block needles and the active hour on the ring. Nothing else glows, including on hover.

rules.name: The Bolted-On Rule
rules.body: Anything that reads as a plate carries its fixings. A brass surface without rivets is a swatch, not a plate.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: The page has a single authored gesture, the arm coming off danger. Everything else moves only as a 160ms response to the pointer. Nothing animates in a way that delays the phone number.

rules.name: The Object Not Card Rule
rules.body: A repeating set belongs to one drawn object with rows keyed to it, not to a grid of boxes. If a set of items would become cards, find the instrument they sit on.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Floor
rules.body: Under prefers-reduced-motion all animation and transition collapse to 0.001ms, the lever's swing and nudge are cancelled outright, and smooth scrolling is off. Every state must remain legible with no motion at all.

dos: Do render enamel as a material: a specular sweep as the first background layer of every maroon field, the /enamel.svg speckle through .enamel::after at soft-light 0.55, and chipped edges where it is bolted.
Do give maroon whole regions to carry, and let iron and hairlines do the structure between them.
Do engrave dark on brass (#1c1408) and bolt every plate with rivets at both ends.
Do confine Martian Mono to measurements: hour numerals, the live time, and the frame's number plates.
Do reach for Archivo's wdth axis for signage proportions instead of adding a display face.
Do draw light rather than source photography: the three boxlight assets are re-authored per orientation, and a portrait frame gets the portrait asset, never a cover-crop of the landscape one.
Do keep every call target at 44px or more and one phone number reachable without scrolling at 390px.
Do cancel the lever swing and every transition under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use maroon as an accent: a tint, a bar, a small highlight, or a badge. It is signage or it is absent.
Don't set text in brass on maroon; it fails contrast, and the plate face is the only place brass carries letters.
Don't introduce a hue outside iron, enamel, maroon, brass and the two lamp glasses. The five frame-paint colours are a client authorisation bounded to the lever stocks and their row spots.
Don't glow anything that is not lamp glass or a block needle.
Don't exceed a 5px corner radius on a rectangular surface; only genuinely round hardware gets a circle.
Don't publish a rating, a review, a testimonial or an aggregateRating: no source exists and none may be invented. The same discipline governs photography of this business.
Don't turn a repeating set into a card grid where a drawn object and keyed rows will carry it.
Don't add a second authored animation, or any motion that stands between the visitor and the number.
